source_name: Verified Market Research — Hungary POS Terminal Market report
why_relevant: A second, independent syndicated sizing of the Hungarian POS terminal market (2025-2033 horizon) — valuable mainly as a cross-check on Mordor's CAGR and vendor list rather than as a standalone authority.

source_name: Finovate — Finovate Global (Eastern Europe editions)
source_subtype: international fintech media / regional round-up column
why_relevant: Recurring regional round-up column that explicitly bundles Hungary with other Eastern European markets, covering funding rounds, payments launches and bank-modernisation deals — a cheap weekly sweep that surfaces smaller Hungarian vendors missed by the majors.

source_name: The Recursive — CEE fintech channel
why_relevant: English-language CEE-focused outlet with named fintech reporters; covers Hungarian scale-ups (SEON, Tresorit) and regional regulatory/association debates involving Hungarian fintech bodies. Fills the gap between Hungarian domestic press and global trade titles.

source_name: Disruption Banking — Hungary/CEE banking features
why_relevant: Publishes standalone English features on the Hungarian ecosystem (e.g. 'Is Hungary's Fintech Ecosystem Growing Today?', August 2026) and vendor-selection stories (OTP–Intellect). Interview-heavy, so it captures named executives and rationale that press releases omit.

source_name: Financial IT — vendor announcement portal
why_relevant: Carries vendor-issued announcements about Hungarian bank selections (Intellect Digital Core at OTP) in near-full press-release form. Low editorial filtering means high vendor-detail density — good for capturing scope/module wording — but must be read as vendor marketing.

source_name: Vendor newsrooms as the upstream of international coverage (iGCB / Intellect Design example)
source_subtype: vendor corporate newsroom (upstream of trade media)
why_relevant: The international trade coverage in this cell is largely reprinted from vendor newsrooms. Going upstream to the vendor's own Hungary announcement page gives the fullest, earliest and most detailed version (contract conditionality language, module names, subsidiary rollout scope such as DSK Bank).

source_name: Chambers and Partners — Fintech 2026 Global Practice Guide: Hungary chapter
why_relevant: Annual English-language expert chapter written by Hungarian law firms: maps the regulatory perimeter, licence types, incumbent and challenger actors and market structure. A rare free, professionally-edited English overview refreshed yearly — excellent for actor-map and terminology building.

source_name: Company/ecosystem databases with Hungary filters (F6S, ensun, Dealroom, CB Insights)
why_relevant: Structured English-language listings of Hungarian fintech companies and of bank-affiliated investors (e.g. MKB Fintechlab, the incubator tied to what is now the MBH Bank group). Chiefly valuable as an actor-discovery pointer to feed back into media searches; company-count claims are unreliable.

source_name: Monri Payments blog — republished The Paypers CEE expert view
source_subtype: vendor blog mirror of trade-media analysis
why_relevant: Illustrates a recurring pattern worth exploiting: paywalled or hard-to-find Paypers expert views on CEE payments are republished in full on the contributing vendor's own site. Vendor mirrors are therefore a practical free route into gated international analyst commentary covering Hungary's region.

source_name: MNB Intézménykereső (Search of market participants / institution finder)
why_relevant: Canonical searchable register of every MNB-licensed or registered financial organisation in Hungary, including payment institutions (pénzforgalmi intézmény), e-money issuers (elektronikuspénz-kibocsátó intézmény), credit institutions and their agents. This is the master actor list from which every other HU banking/payments scout can snowball vendor, competitor and partner names.

source_name: MNB Piaci szereplők keresése (hub page for all registers)
why_relevant: Hub page that enumerates every MNB register: general institution search, intermediaries (közvetítők) search, special databases, and cross-border activity lists. Single best entry point to discover which registers exist at all.

source_name: MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés (Payment Systems Report), annual series
why_relevant: Flagship annual report describing the Hungarian payment market: card issuing/acquiring infrastructure, POS terminal counts, physical vs online acceptance points, instant payment (AFR/GIROInstant) volumes, and named infrastructure operators (GIRO Zrt., KELER, VIBER). Core evidence for acquirer market structure and POS/terminal estate sizing.

source_name: MNB Statisztika – Pénzforgalmi adatok (payment statistics topic hub)
why_relevant: Quarterly official payment statistics: cards, ATMs, POS terminals, payment accounts, merchant acceptance points, acquirer-side and issuer-side transactions, payment fraud and payment revenues. The quantitative backbone for market sizing of the Hungarian acceptance/terminal market.

source_name: MNB Pénzforgalmi táblakészlet (payment data table set, incl. archive)
why_relevant: The downloadable table set itself (and its archive back to 2001, covering chip migration, card business sector, card fraud). Enables long-run trend analysis of POS/terminal and acceptance-point growth in Hungary.

source_name: MNB – A nyílt bankoláshoz kapcsolódó pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók és harmadik fél szolgáltatók adatai (open banking / PSD2 TPP data)
why_relevant: Consolidated MNB-maintained directory of ASPSPs and registered third-party providers (AISP/PISP/CISP) with API and contact details. Directly names Hungarian open-banking fintechs (e.g. KBOSS.hu, Billingo, Nyíltbankolás Zrt., Aggreg8) that are potential partners, competitors or channel players for payments vendors.

source_name: MNB Felügyelet – Pénzforgalmi intézmények adatszolgáltatás page
why_relevant: Sets out the reporting obligations imposed on payment institutions — reveals what data exists on every PSP (and therefore what can later be requested or found in aggregate publications). Useful for understanding data provenance and gaps.

source_name: MNB Engedélyezés – Pénzforgalmi intézmény / tevékenységi engedély guidance
why_relevant: Explains licensing categories and requirements for payment institutions and e-money institutions — needed to correctly interpret and segment register entries (full vs limited PI, EMI, registered AISP). Includes downloadable licensing guides.

source_name: MNB Határozatok és végzések keresése (supervisory decisions search)
why_relevant: Searchable database of MNB licensing, enforcement, market-supervision and consumer-protection decisions, filterable by period, sector and type. Licensing decisions reveal new market entrants, ownership changes and outsourcing/agent arrangements; enforcement decisions reveal operational weaknesses at named PSPs — a strong indirect signal of vendor and partner relationships.

source_name: MNB Közzétételek portal (kozzetetelek.mnb.hu)
why_relevant: Separate MNB disclosure portal hosting statutory publications (issuer disclosures, supervisory publications). Complementary to the decisions search; worth mapping for structured disclosure feeds.

source_name: MNB Azonnali fizetés (AFR) topic pages
why_relevant: MNB's own hub on the instant payment system (AFR) and the qvik QR/deeplink payment brand — describes mandated participation of ~35 PSPs, central infrastructure operated by GIRO Zrt., and rollout milestones. Key for identifying which technology suppliers and PSPs sit on the AFR/qvik value chain.

source_name: MNB Felvigyázás (oversight of VIBER, BKR, KELER, KELER KSZF)
why_relevant: Names and characterises Hungary's financial market infrastructure operators — MNB (VIBER RTGS), GIRO Zrt. (BKR/GIROInstant), KELER (CSD/settlement), KELER KSZF (CCP) — plus oversight assessments and interactive quarterly turnover tables. Canonical infrastructure actor map for the HU payments stack.

source_name: MNB FinTech és Digitalizációs Jelentés (FinTech and Digitalisation Report)
why_relevant: Annual regulator report on financial-sector digitalisation, including a bank-by-bank digitalisation survey covering >90% of the banking system, fintech landscape mapping and technology adoption. Rich for vendor/technology adoption signals and case-study material.

source_name: MNB Innovation Hub / Regulatory Sandbox (Pénzügyi Innovációs Platform)
why_relevant: MNB's fintech engagement channel and Innovative Financial Testing Environment (Innovatív Pénzügyi Tesztkörnyezet, IPT). Sandbox participants and Innovation Hub news items identify emerging Hungarian payment innovators and bank-fintech partnerships early, before they appear in registers.

source_name: MNB Aranykönyv (Golden Book) – institution-level supervisory data
why_relevant: Institution-by-institution supervisory data (balance sheet, P&L, key indicators) for credit institutions, financial undertakings AND payment institutions, investment firms, insurers. Now interactive plus XLSX. This is the single best source for sizing and ranking individual Hungarian PSPs/competitors.

source_name: MNB Statisztika – Publikációs témák (statistics topic index)
why_relevant: Master index of every MNB statistical publication theme (payment data, supervisory statistics, financial institutions' balance sheets, methodologies). Use it to discover datasets not surfaced by search.

source_name: MNB Hungarian cross-border service providers list (EN)
why_relevant: English-language MNB list of Hungarian payment institutions and e-money institutions passporting services cross-border. Identifies which Hungarian PSPs operate regionally — relevant for competitor footprint mapping beyond HU.

source_name: MNB Sajtószoba – sajtóközlemények (press releases)
why_relevant: MNB press releases announce report publications, licensing milestones, AFR/qvik anniversaries and statistics, and Financial Stability Board positions on the payment system. Cheap high-frequency change-detection layer over the slower register/report sources.

source_name: Hitelintézeti Szemle (MNB's peer-reviewed Financial and Economic Review)
why_relevant: MNB-published academic journal carrying policy-relevant analyses of Hungarian payments, fintech regulation and card-market economics (e.g. interchange fee studies). Provides analytical depth and named-market context that the statistical tables lack.
